v.rationale:
I ranked impl-1 first, impl-3 second and impl-2 third. All three test suites pass (17, 15 and 17 tests). All three get the main requirements right: a 201 response with only `token`, 422 for a missing field, 401 with the exact message, a per-email-and-IP throttle that ignores case, revoking only the current token, and an exact /me body.

The probes found one bug in all three. The throttle key reads `email` before validation runs, so sending `email` as an array crashes the limiter with a 500 instead of a 422.

The focus area asks for correct status codes for every client, and here impl-1 stands apart. It is the only one that configured `redirectGuestsTo` so that API guests get a 401. In impl-2 and impl-3, an unauthenticated DELETE or /me request without an Accept: application/json header returns a 500 because the `login` route doesn't exist. impl-1's tests cover that case.

impl-3 and impl-1 are close on idioms: both use `validated()`, an invokable MeController and a named limiter. impl-3 has nicely structured describe blocks but adds a little noise to its tests. impl-2 is the leanest, but it passes Stringable objects into where(), Hash::check() and createToken(string), which only works through implicit coercion. It also moves the existing /user route outside the task's scope, and its tests are slightly weaker. That puts it last.
